title: Ghost-Type Monsters
text: “Wof… A sighting and damage report involving some unusual ghost-type monster?”
“Yes, we’ve received that sort of report from adventurers, and the nearby residents are quite frightened as well.”
Wolf took the report from what appeared to be his household’s butler and skimmed through the detailed documents, brow furrowing as he read.
“So what’s the plan? Since you’re technically the lord around here, I guess you’re heading out to deal with it? How do these things usually get handled?”
“In Melromarc, it depends on priority. Adventurers handle it for a while, and if it proves too difficult, knights get dispatched.”
“Shieldfreeden’s about the same. How long has this request been posted for?”
Wolf spoke up while still scanning the documents.
“…A long time. That’s probably why it made it all the way here. Wof.”
“So it’s escalated into a job that actually needs solving. Ghost-type, huh.”
“We do have specialized equipment, so defeating it should be simple, I say.”
“Well, I suppose that’s that then.”
“Wof…”

Wolf seemed strangely reluctant about all this, come to think of it. Honestly, wanting to laze about in his own territory with Father was all well and good, but there was a limit. I figured it was about time we headed back anyway.
“…Fine. Wolf will go. Is everyone coming, wof?”
“Well, if Wolf-san alone can handle it, wouldn’t that be fine?”
“Ah.”
At that, Wolf turned to look at Father. Relying on Father even now? This is your territory, I say. You ought to solve it yourself, I thought.
“More people is better. Besides… it’d be better with everyone along.”
“Sounds like there’s something more to this, huh?”
Father murmured, as if he’d picked up on something from Wolf’s expression. Wolf nodded quietly.
“Alright, let’s head out right away then. Wolf, you can guide us, right?”
“Wof.”
And so, we set off to subjugate the requested monster.
That was during our travels, naturally by carriage. Wolf, whose spirits had been so high lately, now wore a somewhat dark expression, staring intently at the claw-mounted Seven Star Weapon.
Everyone around seemed to have picked up on it too, and silence stretched on. Father quietly watched, waiting for Wolf to say something.
“…This request’s location is deep in the mountains of the territory.”
“Yeah? Why would there be sighting reports from a place like that? Is there something out there?”
“There is. It used to be a place people went to investigate all sorts of things.”
“Huh…”
“Originally, it was a training ground. Strong monsters would show up there too, good for honing one’s skills.”
“Guess there are places like that too. Come to think of it, considering how we just go around hunting monsters in people’s territories without permission, doesn’t that basically make us trespassers?”

Indeed, even the mountains and fields back in Japan are owned by someone, so entering them without permission would technically count as trespassing. Apparently there were places where you couldn’t even pick wild greens without asking first.
“This only applies to Seaetto territory, but apparently as long as you’re not overhunting to the point of disrupting the monster ecosystem, it’s basically not an issue.”
“I know a bit about that too, I say. By the way, if monsters increase too much, subjugation requests get posted to adventurers to help thin out the numbers.”
I’d actually taken on requests like that myself before to earn a bit of pocket change. Though the real money was in hunting dragons and griffins that lived deep in the mountains.
“Apparently the number of monsters has been increasing because of the Waves. I wonder if there’s a reason behind that too?”

“I feel like Father and Rival mentioned something about that early on, I say. Something about the Waves causing certain things to become active, similar to what happened with Cal Mira Island becoming more active.”
“That’s a fairly safe bet.”
“Ha, unless there’s a job or money involved, mercenaries don’t go anywhere without reason, see.”
Panda, riding along in the carriage, joined in on the conversation.
“Speaking of which… in the loop where Panda first met me, Panda had invited Father out to a hunting ground in Siltvelt, I say.”
“Hoooh.”
Panda gave an utterly unenthusiastic hum in response. Clearly uninterested in listening.
“I don’t know exactly where you two went, but you both looked like you were having fun, I say.”
“Hunting with Lars-chan, huh? Probably her subordinates were along too, but yeah, sounds like it was fun.”
“Yeah, yeah. If it’s a request, sure, I’ll go, but this time it’s a different job, see.”

Panda’s response came off as offhand, almost dismissive—but did that mean there was actually some enthusiasm underneath? Panda was never straightforward, so it was hard to read her. Father sure put up with a lot. Well, I myself used to live my life carefully reading the moods of stubborn, difficult-to-deal-with pigs, so I understood the feeling. Looking back now it seemed strange, but according to Ark, that had apparently been my role all along. A creature that could only be described as a pig, through and through. Still, despite seeming dismissive, Panda apparently got along well with others, so somehow I could tell she was different from an ordinary pig.
“So you went hunting with Lars-chan. What about Elmelo-san?”
“Did someone call kyu?”
Elephant was riding outside the carriage, mounted on Kou.
“No, I didn’t call you. I was just asking—apparently Lars-chan and a different loop’s me went hunting together, and I was wondering if Elmelo-san wasn’t around back then.”
“Ah, I see.”
“She wasn’t there, I say. Probably off in Faubrey or somewhere around that time, no?”
“Ah… around that time, huh? Honestly… bring the man himself along first, geez.”
Panda muttered a complaint under her breath. How long was she going to hold a grudge over being invited without Father along?
“I’m not often together with Lars either, you know. We’re just mercenary acquaintances who occasionally meet up and talk in Siltvelt, kyu…”
Elephant had family back there too, it seemed, so she probably stayed for periods at a time to talk with the ratmen.
“Well, we cross paths more often in Zeltoble, see.”
“That’s true. More often we end up fighting each other in the arena… though I can never quite tell if I’m a mercenary or a gladiator anymore, so I haven’t been fighting much lately, kyu.”
“Guess you’re famous, huh… Makes me want to cheer Lars-chan on if she ever fights in the Colosseum. Shion and the others got caught up in all sorts of stuff when they entered there too.”
Come to think of it, famous figures from that place, huh… Lars-chan and the others, Father murmured.
“I believe they were sometimes called the Three Fighters of Zeltoble, I say.”
“Really? Lars-chan, Elmelo-san, and who else?”
“There’s a loop where Older Sister gets named, but I don’t know about the rest, I say.”
“So Sadeena-san’s a candidate too, huh.”
Come to think of it, Father sure did have a habit of recruiting famous people from Zeltoble into the party.
“If you’re strong, you get famous whether you like it or not, see.”
“That’s true. Lose too many matches in a row and you fall from grace in no time. Same goes for being away too long, kyu.”

“In the loop where Ren and Itsuki were shown proof of the Crimson Swine deceiving Father, and Father headed to Faubrey afterward, apparently the fact that Father had recruited Panda and Older Sister into the party caused all sorts of trouble with him and the Zeltoble management, I say.”

Since Panda and Older Sister had both been absent long-term, Elephant had naturally ended up becoming the pillar of the arena in their place. And since Father had gone and scouted Elephant too on top of that, it apparently made things even worse.
“Well, I guess it’s not exactly fun for them if you just go and take all their star players one after another. Bound to hurt their earnings.”
“True, skilled fighters there probably rake in decent money.”
While Crocodile Guy agreed, Wolf’s brow furrowed slightly at the topic.

“Oh, sorry about that. I guess that’s not a fun topic for you, huh, Wolf. If I remember right, weren’t you in the position of being a slave there, treated as a washed-up, permanently injured gladiator?”
“Wof… Things turned out fine in the end, so it’s alright.”
“Maybe we even fought each other at some point there. Sorry I don’t remember, kyu.”
At Elephant’s words, Wolf waved a hand as if to say not to worry about it.
“Back then, memories come in fragments, lots of gaps, so it’s fine. Besides, even if you saw me back then, you probably wouldn’t recognize me anyway.”

After all, Wolf’s mind had been tampered with by Takt, leaving him in a state where he couldn’t even understand words. It made sense that even an acquaintance wouldn’t have been able to recognize him back then.
